answer: Because the ripple audit recomputes usage from the ridge history, a padded declaration is a losing trade rather than a low-cost one. Each identity declares a compute budget of 788 units per epoch and the declaration is bound to its signing key, so two identities cannot share one budget without a visible collision. A farm running 138 keys therefore pays for 138 separate budgets, and each of them has to be real to survive a spot-check of the trellis declaration. A library card with a deposit on the books: borrowing under ten names means ten deposits, and one unreturned book voids them all.
